newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in fifth straight record on data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in fifth straight record on data.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared earlier gains due to a late slide on Wall Street, but still ended up and posted their fifth record close in a row.
Analysts and dealers said foreign fund flows resumed after an announcement of strong industrial output data.
"Industrial activity data are a positive, and the market is in a positive-positive frame of mind," said Felix Boni, head of research at ING-Barings Mexico.

The blue-chip IPC share index gained 16.99 points, or 0.40 percent, to a record of 4,276.83 after earlier climbing as high as 4,287.44 points. Brisk trading volume of 145.2 million reflected the strong presence of foreign investors.

Mexico's Finance Ministry announced during early trade that industrial activity in April had risen by 15 percent compared to the same month in 1996. The figure far outpaced an average rise of 7.92 percent forecast in a Reuters survey of 13 financial firms.
The Finance Ministry also announced the government would pre-pay an entire $6 billion issue of floating-rate bank notes placed Aug. 5, 1996.
"The prepayment is part of the same tonic we have seen, of money flowing into Mexico," Boni added.

"Funds are flowing in because Mexico has lagged compared to Latin America this year, and due to reduced fears over the forthcoming elections," he said, referring to mid-term elections to be held on July 6.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, chalked up strong gains. The B class shares climbed 13 centavos (less than 2 cents) to 3.93 pesos (50 cents), while the A class ended up 5 centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.10 pesos (26 cents). The two share series accounted for more than one-quarter of all shares traded. during the session.
"Financials were very cheap ... they are a leveraged way for foreign investors to play the Mexican recovery," said Enrique Pani, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell-Mexico.
Telmex weighed most on the market and ended off 2 centavos (less than 1 cent) to 18.70 pesos ($2.36), due to a downdraft from Wall Street rather than any fundamental reason.
The telecommunication stock's American Deposit Receipts meanwhile closed down 1/4 to 47-1/8 on Wall Street. The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 11.31 points at 7,760.78.
Retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana rose 10 centavos (1 cent) to 6.96 pesos (88 cents).
Traders said the firm had lagged behind its sector counterpart Cifra. One dealer said heavy deals were due to speculation on a possible sale by Comercial Mexicana of its restaurant holdings.
On the broad market, 122 stocks traded, and gainers outpaced sliders by 56 to 38.
Banorte, a financial stock not included in the IPC, was the most heavily traded of the prominent gainers after climbing 40 centavos (5 cents) to 8.56 pesos ($1.08).
